Rarity.rationale: Obtainable: not in the grab bag (Ancient), granted by the ported Neow event -- `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b12.py b12-pool` reports granted_by=['sts2_rl/events/neow.py'].

AfterObtained.rationale: Pomander.cs:17-24 selects Cards(1) upgradable deck cards and upgrades each; pomander.py:14-16 does the same through run.select_cards('upgrade', run.upgradable_cards(), 1) and card.upgrade(). Both the IsUpgradable filter (guard N1, the bug-class-14 check, cleared by execution) and the auto-select-when-the-list-is-short semantics (guard N2) match, and the select-then-mutate ordering matches (guard N3). Rollup of N1-N5 per binding rule 4: the worst verdict among them is the presentation waiver, so this hook carries no divergence.

guards.what: N1 (bug class 14, CLEARED by execution): the sim's Card.upgrade() has no IsUpgradable guard, but Pomander's candidate list carries it
guards.rationale: C#'s CardCmd.Upgrade skips any card whose IsUpgradable is false (src/Core/Commands/CardCmd.cs:271-276, `if (!card.IsUpgradable) continue;`) and the sim's Card.upgrade() (cards/base.py:146-148) is a bare `upgrade_level += 1` plus _on_upgrade with no guard at all, so every sim caller must supply its own filter -- PROMPT.md bug class 14, which fired as a LIVE gap on relic/astrolabe and relic/bone_tea. Pomander does supply it: run.upgradable_cards() (run.py:368-369) is `[c for c in self.deck if c.is_upgradable]` and Card.is_upgradable (cards/base.py:167-170) is CardModel.IsUpgradable's `CurrentUpgradeLevel < MaxUpgradeLevel`. That mirrors the source, which filters in the same place -- CardSelectCmd.FromDeckForUpgrade takes `PileType.Deck.GetPile(player).Cards.Where(c => c.IsUpgradable)` (src/Core/Commands/CardSelectCmd.cs:442) -- so both sides filter the candidate list and both are safe. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b12.py b12-cutters): a deck of 10 upgradable cards plus a curse_of_the_bell (max_upgrade_level 0) offers 10 candidates and leaves the curse at upgrade_level 0. This is also the correction .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md sweep D records: its first version over-reported pomander because it looked for the guard in a 3-line window rather than the enclosing function. NOTE per binding rule 7: CardCmd.cs, CardSelectCmd.cs, cards/base.py, run.py and content-relic-sweeps.md are NOT hashed by this record.

The single-argument CardSelectorPrefs constructor sets MinSelect = MaxSelect = selectCount and therefore RequireManualConfirmation = false (src/Core/CardSelection/CardSelectorPrefs.cs:62-77), so FromDeckForUpgrade's `if (list.Count <= prefs.MinSelect && !RequireManualConfirmation) enumerable = list;` (CardSelectCmd.cs:448-451) auto-takes the whole list when the deck has one or fewer upgradable cards. RunState.select_cards clamps identically with `count = min(count, len(candidates))` and returns [] for an empty candidate list (run.py:371-390). CardsVar(1) (Pomander.cs:15) read as IntValue is the pinned non-ascension value -- no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file -- and the sim's literal 1 matches; checked against the C# rather than the port's docstring per PROMPT.md bug class 19. WHICH card is chosen is a player decision on both sides (the sim delegates to run.card_selector and falls back to a uniform run-RNG sample), so the selection itself is not a fidelity question. NOTE per binding rule 7: CardSelectorPrefs.cs, CardSelectCmd.cs and run.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: N5: Pomander.cs overrides no HasUponPickupEffect, so RelicModel.IsTradable treats this consumed one-shot relic as tradable -- and the port copies the omission faithfully
guards.rationale: Recorded as an entry rather than a divergence because the port and the source AGREE: Pomander.cs declares Rarity, CanonicalVars and AfterObtained only (25 lines), and pomander.py declares no has_upon_pickup_effect either, so Relic.has_upon_pickup_effect stays at its False default (relics/base.py:96). Both codebases therefore consider a spent Pomander tradable on the has_upon_pickup_effect axis. It cannot matter here because Relic.is_tradable also excludes ANCIENT rarity outright (relics/base.py:134-136, mirroring RelicModel.IsTradable), and Pomander is Ancient -- so the relic is untradable for the other reason on both sides. Worth an entry because the three sibling pickup relics in this same batch (phial_holster, precarious_shears, precise_scissors) DO declare it while pomander and preserved_fog do not, exactly matching which C# files override the property; a reviewer who assumed the four should look alike would 'fix' two correct ports. NOTE per binding rule 7: relics/base.py is not hashed here.

guards.what: N3: `CardCmd.Upgrade(item)` is called per selected card in a loop after the whole selection resolves (Pomander.cs:20-23); the sim upgrades inside the comprehension loop (pomander.py:15-16)
guards.rationale: Same structure -- select first, then upgrade the returned set -- and with one card selected the loop shape cannot differ. Checked because a select-then-act ordering matters when the selection screen itself reads the deck (an upgrade performed mid-selection would change later candidates); both sides materialise the selection before mutating (C# with `.ToList()` at Pomander.cs:19, the sim because select_cards returns a list). CardCmd.Upgrade's `if (CombatManager.Instance.IsEnding) return;` early bail (CardCmd.cs:267-270) has no sim analogue and cannot apply: AfterObtained runs out of combat.

guards.what: N4: no other override -- and no Flash / CanonicalVars beyond CardsVar(1)
guards.rationale: CanonicalVars / the UpgradeSelectionPrompt LocString / CardCmd.Upgrade's preview style and NUpgradePreview tweening are presentation only -- prompt text, the card-preview animation and the relic bar. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.
